display.purpose: Home hero headline only. Fluid clamp(2.5rem, 1.1rem + 4.2vw, 4.75rem), about 76px at 1440; the break falls after the dash.

h1.purpose: Inner-page titles, 404 and error. Fluid clamp(2.375rem, 1.2rem + 3.4vw, 4.25rem).

h2.purpose: Every section's station heading. Fluid clamp(2rem, 1.2rem + 2.4vw, 3.5rem); service titles on /services use clamp(1.75rem, 1.1rem + 1.8vw, 2.75rem).

h3.purpose: Line names, founders' names, the hub. Fluid clamp(1.3125rem, 1.08rem + 0.7vw, 1.75rem).

lead.purpose: The paragraph under a heading: ink in the hero (34ch), Platform Grey under section headings (44ch). Fluid clamp(1.1875rem, 1rem + 0.55vw, 1.5rem).

body.purpose: Running text at 66ch. Numerals lining throughout, tabular for years, hours and counts.

meta.purpose: Sublines, hours, notes and list descriptions, in Platform Grey.

label.purpose: Line badges and caption labels; nav stations use 700 at 1rem.

chip.purpose: Tech chips; the language switch uses 800 at this size.

shadows.name: train-lift
shadows.purpose: Under the capsule trains on the page rail and the process track.

shadows.name: floating-caption
shadows.purpose: The white caption pill sitting on a poster.

shadows.name: header-hairline
shadows.purpose: The solid header's bottom edge: a rule, not elevation.

shadows.name: ring-frame
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: the 2px ink ring around pictures, ghost pills, tags, filters and the language switch.

shadows.name: ring-station
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: a heading station's ring (4px nav, 7px line stops and process, 8px map and hub, 9px contact stations; #dcdde0 before it is reached).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default curve: hovers, rings lighting, the red sweep, reveals, lines drawing themselves.

motion.name: ease-wipe
motion.purpose: A train pulling out and braking: only for things that cross the whole frame (the poster wipe).

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: The mobile sheet closing; the current-page station sliding to the new page.

motion.name: ease-exit
motion.purpose: The outgoing page in a view transition (0.26s, fading and rising 10px).

motion.name: ease-train
motion.purpose: Map trains easing at each end of their back-and-forth run (5-20s per loop).

motion.name: duration-ring
motion.purpose: Station rings lighting, the red core growing, arrow nudges.

motion.name: duration-sweep
motion.purpose: The red sweep through a pill, the FAQ answer opening, the header hiding.

motion.name: duration-sheet
motion.purpose: The mobile sheet's circular reveal (0.55s closing).

motion.name: duration-wipe
motion.purpose: The poster train crossing the frame.

motion.name: duration-draw
motion.purpose: The hero map drawing itself once (service lines draw in 1.2s).

components.name: Service Lines and Hub
components.description: «Четыре линии — одна команда»: each service is a 14px line in its own colour with four ink-ringed stations, and all four end at the hub, a white interchange panel with an 8px ink ring. Shown in the drawn state every line rests in; on the site each line draws itself once from the left on first view (1.2s, 0.18s apart). The block closes on the arrow link to /services.
components.html:
MAX и Telegram

  1. Разработка Mini App для MAX и Telegram
  2. Чат-боты для MAX с навигацией и автоматизацией
  3. Подключение платёжных систем (ЮKassa и др.)
  4. Личные кабинеты, CRM и аналитика внутри мессенджера

ИИ-интеграции

  1. ИИ-ассистенты в чат-ботах MAX и Telegram
  2. ИИ-консультант и умный поиск на сайте
  3. Обработка заявок, писем и документов
  4. Интеграция с 1С, CRM и базой знаний

Веб

  1. Проектирование структуры и логики
  2. Дизайн и вёрстка
  3. Разработка функционала
  4. Запуск и настройка хостинга

iOS

  1. Проектирование архитектуры и логики приложения
  2. Дизайн интерфейса
  3. Разработка и тестирование
  4. Подготовка к публикации и релиз в App Store

Пересадка: общий backend

Каждая линия опирается на собственный backend и интеграции, которые мы пишем сами.

  • Node.js
  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • PostgreSQL
  • LLM
  • 1С МИС
  • ЮKassa

components.description: The 4:5 poster beside the works list: Enamel Tint ground, a 2px ink ring drawn above the picture, a floating white caption pill. When the project changes, a band of its line colour crosses the frame on the braking curve; hovering replays it here.
components.css: .ds-poster { position: relative; width: min(100%, 320px); aspect-ratio: 4 / 5; margin: 0; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 28px; background: var(--tint, #f4f4f2); color: var(--ink, #16171a); font-family: var(--font, 'Golos Text', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-poster::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 5; border-radius: inherit; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--ink, #16171a); pointer-events: none; } .ds-poster--max { --line: var(--red, #e4251b); } .ds-poster__wipe { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: 0; z-index: 3; width: 18%; background: var(--line); transform: translateX(-100%); pointer-events: none; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-poster:hover .ds-poster__wipe { animation: ds-poster-train 0.75s var(--ease-wipe, cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.25, 1)) both; } } @keyframes ds-poster-train { from { transform: translateX(-100%); } to { transform: translateX(555.6%); } } .ds-poster__cap { position: absolute; left: 18px; right: 18px; bottom: 18px; z-index: 4; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 12px 18px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--paper, #ffffff); box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(22, 23, 26, 0.14); font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.9375rem; line-height: 1; } .ds-poster__badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-poster__badge i { width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--line); flex: none; } .ds-poster__year { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums; }

components.name: FAQ Timetable
components.description: A timetable list (2px ink rule on top, hairline rows) with a 44px ring toggle: hover fills it ink; open turns it 45° into a red cross and the answer slides open.
components.html:
• Зависит от сложности проекта. Простой бот для MAX или Telegram и большое iOS-приложение — разные объёмы работы. Напишите с описанием задачи, и мы дадим конкретную оценку.

  • Да. Подключаем языковые модели к сайтам, чат-ботам MAX и Telegram и внутренним системам.
components.css: .ds-faq { max-width: 980px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; border-top: 2px solid var(--ink, #16171a); color: var(--ink, #16171a); font-family: var(--font, 'Golos Text', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-faq__item { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #e6e7e9); } .ds-faq h3 { margin: 0; } .ds-faq__q { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 44px; align-items: center; gap: 20px; width: 100%; padding: 24px 0; border: 0; background: none; color: inherit; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; font-family: inherit; font-weight: 800; font-size: clamp(1.125rem, 1rem + 0.45vw, 1.375rem); line-height: 1.25; letter-spacing: -0.015em; } .ds-faq__q:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--blue, #0a6fd8); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 6px; } .ds-faq__icon { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 50%; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--ink, #16171a); transition: background-color 0.25s, color 0.25s, transform 0.45s var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)); } .ds-faq__icon svg { width: 18px; height: 18px; } .ds-faq__q:hover .ds-faq__icon { background: var(--ink, #16171a); color: var(--paper, #ffffff); } .ds-faq__item.is-open .ds-faq__icon { transform: rotate(45deg); background: var(--red, #e4251b); color: var(--paper, #ffffff); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--red, #e4251b); } .ds-faq__a { display: grid; grid-template-rows: 0fr; transition: grid-template-rows 0.45s var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)); } .ds-faq__item.is-open .ds-faq__a { grid-template-rows: 1fr; } .ds-faq__a > div { overflow: hidden; } .ds-faq__a p { max-width: 70ch; margin: 0; padding: 0 64px 28px 0; color: var(--ink-2, #565961); font-size: 1.0625rem; line-height: 1.55; }

narrative.overview:
«Схема линий»: the site is a metro scheme printed on white enamel. StackLab's services are coloured lines, the systems a client already runs (MAX, 1С МИС, ЮKassa, live schedules, an AI assistant) are stations, and every page is one route the reader rides from heading to heading. The world's whole vocabulary is the scheme's own: thick round-capped lines, white stations with heavy ink rings, small white trains, ink signage, and a legend of coloured discs. Case images and the founders' portraits are the destinations the lines lead to.

The register is municipal signage set for a formal Russian business reader. One heavy grotesque with full Cyrillic speaks at 800 weight, big and tightly tracked; reading text stays plain and neutral; lists read like timetables; white ground does the separating. Colour is rationed by meaning: red is the route and whatever is lit or current, and violet, blue and green only ever name their lines. Depth is drawn with rings and rules rather than lit with shadows. Motion is the scheme coming alive (lines draw themselves once, trains run, the route fills red behind the reader), and every frame is complete and legible at rest.

The world refuses two category defaults by name: the dark agency showreel (black ground, neon accent, WebGL blob, kinetic type) and the white SaaS template (a centred hero over rows of three icon cards). A product constraint sets its budget: the site must stay fast on weak machines and slow mobile connections, so everything is drawn in CSS and inline SVG. The existing StackLab logo stays unchanged, top left (44px tall, 36px below 1100px) and in the footer (52px).
keyCharacteristics: White enamel ground with ink signage; no dark sections.
Four line colours, one per service line; red doubles as the lit route.
Stations are white discs with heavy ink rings; interchanges are larger rings.
Thick round-capped strokes; on a scheme, segments run horizontal, vertical or at 45° only.
One typeface, Golos Text, with signage at 800 and tight tracking.
Every content page is one route: a rail in the left gutter, a station at every section heading.
Flat surfaces: rings and rules, never a drop shadow on anything static.
Pills for every control; 26–28px rounded frames for every picture.

rules.name: The One Colour, One Line Rule
rules.body: Each colour draws one line, and wherever a service, project or direction is named the mapping is fixed: MAX & Telegram Mini Apps and bots red, ИИ-интеграции violet, Web blue, iOS green. Telegram rides the red line with MAX and never gets its own colour. A project's badge, filter dot and poster wipe take its platform's line. A new colour arrives only with a new service line.

rules.name: The Lit Route Rule
rules.body: Route elements have three states: unlit (an Unlit Track ring or track), lit (an ink ring) and here (a red core or a red fill). Progress, the current page and the active item are red; hover darkens to ink or runs red, except on the hero map, where a hovered station fills with its own line's colour.

rules.name: The Enamel Ground Rule
rules.body: Line colours fill lines, discs, badges, the poster's passing train and the red state fills; they never fill a section, card or panel. Surfaces are White Enamel, with Enamel Tint as the only second surface.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Golos Text sets everything: display, signage, body, labels and the station names on the map. Hierarchy comes from weight and size; there is no second family, no serif and no monospace.

rules.name: The Signage Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings, names, station labels and buttons are 800 with negative tracking, from −0.035em at display to −0.018em at title and never tighter. Reading text stays at 400–600; 700 belongs to small labels, links, chips and the founders' pull quote.

rules.name: The Route Rule
rules.body: Every content page is one route. Each section opens with a station heading hung on the rail in the left gutter; the rail runs from the first station to the last, Unlit Track ahead of the reader and red behind, with a white train at the reading line (mid-viewport). Below the hero, content never starts left of the rail indent; a section without a station heading is off the route. Only the home hero (the map is where the route begins) and the 404 and error pages (the broken line) sit outside the rail.

rules.name: The Flat Enamel Rule
rules.body: Static surfaces never cast shadows. A shadow means "this rides on top": trains and floating caption pills only. Borders are rings, not shadows.

rules.name: The Ring Rule
rules.body: Every outline around a shape is an inset ring in ink (Unlit Track before it is reached, red when it is here), drawn inside the element so it never shifts layout: 2px for frames, ghost controls and tags; 3–4px for small toggles, indicators and nav stations; 5–9px for stations and trains, growing with the disc. The only plain borders are the horizontal rules of lists and the footer.

rules.name: The Round-Cap Rule
rules.body: Every visible line end is round, and every segment on a scheme runs horizontal, vertical or at 45°. A line may end square only where it runs under a station or the hub.

dos: Do open every section with a station heading so it hangs on the route, and keep content at the rail indent (72px; 44px on phones).
Do take a line colour only from the line mapping: MAX & Telegram red, ИИ-интеграции violet, Web blue, iOS green.
Do move route stations and tracks through unlit (#dcdde0), lit (ink) and here (red).
Do draw stations as white discs with inset ink rings sized to the disc (16/4, 28/6, 32–34/7, 64/9px).
Do draw scheme lines horizontal, vertical or at 45°, round-capped, with a white casing where one line crosses another without a station.
Do keep calls to action to the ink pill (46, 56 or 64px), the ghost pill and the arrow link.
Do lay out lists as timetables: a 2px ink rule on top, 1px #e6e7e9 hairlines between rows.
Do frame case pictures on Enamel Tint with a 2px inset ink ring at 26–28px radius; contain logos with 7–9% padding and let photographs cover.
Do draw icons as inline SVG on a 24-unit grid with one round-capped stroke (2.6px; 2.8px for the plus).

Do keep every frame complete at rest: lines and stations are drawn by default, motion arms only when reduced motion is off, trains pause off-screen, and durations follow distance (0.18s press, 0.2–0.35s colour and rings, 0.45s sweeps and accordions, 0.75s cross-frame wipes on the braking curve, 1.2–1.5s for lines drawing themselves).
Do theme the browser's own surfaces from the palette: red selection and caret, an ink scrollbar thumb that turns red on hover, and a 3px blue focus ring at 3px offset.
donts: Don't build the dark agency showreel (black ground, neon accent, WebGL blob, kinetic type) or the white SaaS template (a centred hero over rows of three icon cards).
Don't fill a section, card or panel with a line colour, or set running text in one; green and Dim Grey never set text at all.
Don't add a colour without adding a service line, and don't split Telegram off the red line.
Don't give a static surface a drop shadow; only trains and floating caption pills carry the soft ink shadow.
Don't bring in a second typeface, a monospace "tech" voice, or headings below 800.
Don't set a text label above a heading; a line badge sits beside or below the title.
Don't use Unicode arrows or emoji as icons.
Don't reach for WebGL, video or other heavy effects; the world is drawn in CSS and inline SVG so it stays fast on weak devices and slow connections.
